title: Dr Reddy's Wins Exclusive Rights to Distribute Takeda's QDENGA Dengue Vaccine in India
excerpt: The exclusive private-market partnership will make India's first approved dengue vaccine available for pediatric and adult vaccination in the first half of 2027, with Dr Reddy's handling promotion and distribution while Takeda retains manufacturing and public-market rights.
body:
• Dr Reddy's Laboratories has signed an exclusive agreement with Japan's Takeda Pharmaceutical to promote and distribute QDENGA, India's first approved dengue vaccine, in the private market for pediatric and adult vaccination.
  • The vaccine is expected to be available in the first half of 2027, subject to local regulatory processes. QDENGA (TAK-003) is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine approved by the CDSCO in July 2026 for ages 4 to 60, given as two doses three months apart.
  • Reported dengue cases in India have risen 11-fold over two decades; an ICMR surveillance study found all four dengue serotypes co-circulating, with one in 14 patients infected by multiple serotypes at once.
  • Dr Reddy's will exclusively handle private-market promotion, marketing and distribution, while Takeda retains manufacturing, import, legal ownership and public-market rights. No upfront or milestone payments are involved; remaining commercial terms are confidential.

A first-of-its-kind vaccine deal

Takeda Pharmaceutical Company, through its Indian subsidiary Takeda Biopharmaceuticals India, has formalized an exclusive distribution agreement with Dr Reddy's Laboratories under which the Hyderabad-based company will promote and distribute Takeda's dengue vaccine QDENGA across India's private market for pediatric and adult vaccination. The vaccine is expected to become available in the first half of 2027, subject to applicable processes with local authorities.

This is Takeda's second agreement with an Indian company involving QDENGA — the multinational already has a supply tie-up with Biological E, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. QDENGA received marketing authorization from the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) in July 2026 for individuals aged 4 to 60, making it the first dengue vaccine ever approved in India.

Context & Background

Dengue has become one of India's fastest-growing public-health threats. Reported cases are up 11-fold over the past two decades, and a surveillance study by the Indian Council of Medical Research's Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratory found all four dengue serotypes — DENV-1 through DENV-4 — co-circulating across multiple regions, with one in 14 patients infected by more than one serotype at once. That co-circulation matters because secondary infections carry a higher risk of severe disease.

QDENGA (TAK-003) is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine built on a DENV-2 backbone with structural proteins from DENV-1, DENV-3 and DENV-4, covering all four serotypes in a two-dose regimen spaced three months apart. Mahender Nayak, Takeda's Head of Intercontinental Markets, told BusinessLine that the Biological E manufacturing alliance is central to expanding global production capacity for QDENGA and widening access in dengue-endemic countries.

Impact & Analysis

The agreement splits India's market in two. Dr Reddy's takes exclusive responsibility for private-market promotion, marketing and distribution, while Takeda keeps public-market commercialization rights, legal ownership, and control of manufacturing, import, and medical, regulatory and brand strategy. The companies will jointly run disease-awareness campaigns and engage healthcare professionals.

A Parliamentary Committee on Health recently recommended considering a dengue vaccine for India's Universal Immunization Program (UIP). "This reflects the growing recognition of dengue as a significant public health challenge," Nayak said. For now, though, access is private-market only: "While inclusion in India's public immunization program remains an important long-term ambition, private-market availability through Dr Reddy's will provide a pathway for eligible individuals to access the vaccine once it becomes available," the company said.

Diaspora Angle

For NRIs, timing matters as much as the deal itself. Travelers visiting India during the monsoon and post-monsoon months — peak dengue transmission season — face one of the highest exposure risks of any travel-related illness. With the vaccine approved for ages 4 to 60, families sending children to visit grandparents in India will have a new preventive option in private clinics from 2027. The two-dose schedule, three months apart, means starting vaccination well before travel.

What's Next

The immediate milestone is the H1 2027 availability window, contingent on regulatory processes with local authorities. Watch for pricing when Dr Reddy's discloses commercial terms closer to launch — that will determine real accessibility. The longer-term question is whether the Parliamentary Committee's recommendation turns into UIP inclusion, converting dengue vaccination from a private purchase to a publicly funded program. In parallel, Takeda's manufacturing ramp-up with Biological E will show how aggressively it plans to take QDENGA to other dengue-endemic countries.

"As the second-largest vaccine player in India, we believe the introduction of India's first approved dengue vaccine is an important development for the country's healthcare landscape."

— M.V. Ramana, CEO – Global Generics, Dr. Reddy's Laboratories

"This reflects the growing recognition of dengue as a significant public health challenge."

— Mahender Nayak, Head of Intercontinental Markets, Takeda
